flashcard_questions.a: Using motion to induce a potential difference in a conductor.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What must happen for a potential difference to be induced?
flashcard_questions.a: There must be relative movement between a conductor and a magnetic field.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) How does moving a magnet faster change the induced potential difference?
flashcard_questions.a: It increases it, because more field lines are cut per second.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) How does adding more turns to a coil affect the output?
flashcard_questions.a: Each turn adds its own induced voltage, so the output rises.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) How can the direction of an induced current be reversed?
flashcard_questions.a: By reversing the movement, or by reversing the magnet's polarity.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why is there no deflection when a magnet rests inside a coil?
flashcard_questions.a: The magnetic field around the coil is not changing.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Which component gives an alternator its alternating output?
(Higher) Which component makes a dynamo produce direct current?
(Higher) How does a moving-coil microphone produce an electrical signal?
flashcard_questions.a: Sound vibrates a diaphragm and coil, inducing an alternating potential difference.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What makes the cone of a loudspeaker vibrate?
flashcard_questions.a: An alternating force on the voice coil in a magnetic field.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why do transformers only work with alternating current?
flashcard_questions.a: Direct current gives a steady field, which induces nothing in the secondary coil.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why is a transformer core made of soft iron?
flashcard_questions.a: It magnetises and demagnetises easily, transferring the changing field efficiently.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) How do the coils of a step-up transformer compare?
flashcard_questions.a: The secondary coil has more turns than the primary coil.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Vp / Vs = ____ / ____, the transformer turns ratio.
(Higher) Why does the National Grid transmit at very high voltage?
flashcard_questions.a: High voltage means low current, so less energy is wasted as heat.

notes: 15 cards, every one prefixed '(Higher)' because the whole lesson body sits inside a higher-only block. Mix is 2 term→definition (generator effect, induction condition), 3 'what happens if' factor cards (speed, turns, reversing direction), 1 cloze on the turns-ratio equation, 2 component→output cards (slip rings, commutator) with distinct answers, 2 device cards (microphone, loudspeaker), 4 causal cards (stationary magnet, a.c. only, soft iron, National Grid), 1 structural comparison. Dropped the transformer worked example as calculation practice; no single-word answers were used because the '(Higher)' prefix would fail the validator's single-word question pattern.
